title: Start the Year With One Operating Rule
teaser: A short decision rule can be more useful than a long list of resolutions.
full_text: Write one rule you can reuse throughout the year, such as checking capacity before accepting new work or verifying an important file before delivery. Keep it short enough to apply under pressure.

title: See the Real Capacity of the First Week
teaser: An open calendar does not always mean the transition into a new year requires no attention.
full_text: Review this week's work in terms of mental load as well as hours. Build a pace you can sustain instead of filling every open space immediately.

title: Add the First Measurement Point to One Goal
teaser: Progress is easier to evaluate when it has a starting reference.
full_text: Choose one goal you intend to track this year. Record the current value and set the first review date so later changes can be compared with a real baseline.

title: Choose One Source of Truth
teaser: Multiple editable copies of the same information can make current status unclear.
full_text: For one frequently updated piece of information, decide where the primary source will live. Mark other copies as references or archives when possible.

title: Define the Smallest Version of One New Habit
teaser: A starting standard that is too large can make consistency unnecessarily difficult.
full_text: For one new habit, choose a minimum version you could still do on a demanding day. Judge the first weeks by continuity before judging them by ideal performance.

title: Set a Limit Before One Variable Expense Grows
teaser: A boundary chosen before spending can be more useful than regret after the total is known.
full_text: Pick one variable expense category for this month and set a realistic upper limit in advance. Connect the number to actual need and available budget.

title: Review the First Week by Outcomes
teaser: Early-year motivation does not tell you which methods are actually working.
full_text: Look at what you started during the first week. Keep one behavior that produced real progress and reduce one that created activity without enough value.

title: Write the Definition of Done for One Task
teaser: Work can remain open indefinitely when completion has no clear condition.
full_text: For one active task, write the conditions that make it finished. Separate delivery, verification, and approval when those are distinct steps.

title: Test One Assumption With Evidence
teaser: Plans often depend on assumptions that remain invisible until they fail.
full_text: Choose one assumption underneath an important plan today. Use available data, observation, or a small test to check whether it still deserves to be treated as true.

title: Reduce the Preparation Cost of One Recurring Meeting
teaser: Repeated discussions should not require rebuilding the same structure each time.
full_text: Create a stable agenda, decision log, and action area for one recurring meeting. Next time, add only what has actually changed.

title: Put a Review Date on One Temporary Permission
teaser: Access granted for a short need can remain long after the need disappears.
full_text: Review one permission related to a temporary project or shared resource. Add an expiry or review point where the platform allows it.

title: Estimate the Reversal Cost of One Decision
teaser: A reversible choice and a long-term commitment do not need the same amount of analysis.
full_text: For one decision today, estimate how difficult it would be to reverse. If reversal is expensive, spend more effort on validation and alternatives before committing.

title: Measure Waiting Time in One Workflow
teaser: Working time and total delivery time are not the same thing.
full_text: Separate active work from time spent waiting for approval, response, access, or a queue in one process. Make the largest source of delay visible.

title: Define the Condition for Changing One Goal
teaser: Past effort alone is not a reason to continue a goal indefinitely.
full_text: For one goal this year, write the evidence or condition that would make you change the approach, reduce the scope, or stop.

title: Reduce the Number of Midmonth Priorities
teaser: When everything is a priority, the word stops helping with decisions.
full_text: Choose no more than three areas that truly deserve protection for the second half of January. Keep other work visible without treating it all as equally urgent.

title: Close the Repeat Path of One Error
teaser: Fixing a problem once and preventing recurrence are different kinds of work.
full_text: Choose one error you recently resolved. Ask whether a validation, automation, or clearer ownership point could make the same failure less likely to return.

title: Shorten One Message That Needs a Decision
teaser: Too much supporting detail can hide the question that actually needs an answer.
full_text: In one message that requires a decision, make the main question visible near the beginning. Put supporting detail after the decision point instead of before it.

title: Define Required Fields for One Record Type
teaser: Missing information often becomes research work later.
full_text: Choose one type of record you create repeatedly and identify the minimum fields that must always be present. Avoid adding fields that do not serve a clear future use.

title: Break One Repeated Task Into Time Components
teaser: Estimates improve when they are informed by how similar work actually behaves.
full_text: For one repeated task, estimate preparation, execution, and verification separately using recent examples. Use those parts instead of one vague total next time you schedule it.

title: Verify the Freshness of One Important Source
teaser: Information can remain plausible after it has stopped being current.
full_text: Check the publication or update date of one source behind an important decision today. If newer information is needed, do not let an older source stand alone.

title: Do Not Automatically Count Busyness as Success
teaser: A full day can still leave the most valuable outcome untouched.
full_text: At the end of today, look first at whether the most important result moved forward, then at how many tasks were completed. Keep activity and impact separate.

title: Reduce Single-Person Dependency in One Process
teaser: Critical knowledge becomes fragile when too few people can locate or use it.
full_text: Check one important process today and confirm that required access, documentation, and basic steps do not exist only in one person's memory.

title: Close One Small Reversible Decision Faster
teaser: Low-risk choices can become expensive when they wait for heavyweight review.
full_text: Choose one decision that is easy to reverse and limited in impact. If enough information is already available, close it without adding unnecessary approval layers.

title: Name the Owner of One Shared Dataset
teaser: Information without an owner tends to become outdated quietly.
full_text: Choose one shared list or dataset and make responsibility for updates explicit. If ownership changes, record the change where users can see it.

title: Check External Dependencies in One Plan
teaser: Your part being ready does not mean the whole process can move.
full_text: List the approvals, data, deliveries, or access you still depend on for one upcoming task. Add timing margin around the dependency that could delay the whole plan.

title: Shorten One Feedback Loop
teaser: Learning about a problem late usually makes correction more expensive.
full_text: In one piece of work today, consider adding a smaller interim review or early sample so useful feedback arrives before the final delivery.

title: Check Recovery Information for One Critical Account
teaser: Security includes being able to regain access through a method you still control.
full_text: Review the recovery email, phone, or backup method for one important account. Update stale information without exposing recovery details unnecessarily.

title: Classify What Should Remain Open at Month-End
teaser: Not every unfinished item deserves automatic transfer into another month.
full_text: Review January's open work by value, obligation, and relevance. Finish, redefine, schedule, or deliberately drop each meaningful item.

title: Read One Metric Together With Its Side Effects
teaser: Improving one number can damage another part of the system.
full_text: Choose one performance measure you track and ask what happens to quality, cost, or time when that number is pushed higher. Watch for incentives that reward the wrong behavior.

title: Choose One Experiment for February
teaser: Changing many things at once makes it difficult to learn what caused the result.
full_text: Pick one process or habit change to test in February. Record the starting condition and the signal you intend to observe before the experiment begins.

title: Close January With Decisions
teaser: Month-end is useful for deciding the fate of open work, not only counting what finished.
full_text: Record what completed, what carries forward, and what you chose to stop. Give every important February carryover a visible next action and, when possible, a date.
